newsitem.title: CHINA: China says 600 ships delayed as Yangtze blocked.
newsitem.headline: China says 600 ships delayed as Yangtze blocked.

text.p: A blockage along China's Yangtze river delayed some 600 ships for more than two weeks last month, the China Daily said on Saturday.
The newspaper said the vessels had been cleared but the lengthy delays along the inland waterway had been due to repairs on two of the three locks at the Gezhouba dam in Yichang in Hubei province.

It said the disruption was accidental and required emergency repairs at lock number two. It did not give further details but it said added this was one of several similar incidents since the dam was built in 1981.

The newspaper also said that in clearing the delayed vessels authorities gave priority to passenger ships and vessels carrying cargo for the big Three Gorges dam project, which is under way further west along the Yangtze.

"It is very rare that two of the three locks of the dam are out of order at the same time... but the accident needs to be taken seriously, especially as traffic flow increases in future," the newspaper quoted Liang Yingzhan, director of the Office for Three Gorges Navigation under the Ministry of Communications.
The Three Gorges dam, China's largest water control and power project, will be operational in 2009.
